1000642.etyen:
Ultimately from Ancient Greek Κύπρος (Kúpros). The precise route into Norwegian is uncertain. The deeper origin of the Greek name is likewise uncertain; it has traditionally been associated with the island's ancient copper production, while another interpretation connects it with the cypress tree.
The island name appears in Latin aes Cyprium (“Cypriot copper”), later cuprum (“copper”), ultimately the source of Norwegian Bokmål kobber (“copper”).
Compare Greek Κύπρος (Kýpros), Finnish Kypros, Danish Cypern, English Cyprus and Turkish Kıbrıs (“Cyprus”).

1001410.etyen:
An old Norwegian river name. Rygh reconstructs an older form Old Norse *Etn or *Ǫtn, with a derivational *-n- also found in other old river names. The stem may be related either to Old Norse etja (“to urge, drive forward”) or eta (“to eat”). Under the latter interpretation, the name means “the one who eats”, referring to a river that erodes or “eats” its way forward. The river gave its name to Etnedal (“valley and municipality”).
Compare Norwegian Atna (“river in Østerdalen”), which Rygh analyses as a parallel formation.

1003970.etyen: abdisere + -ing, verbal noun of abdisere (“to abdicate”). First part from Latin abdicāre, a form of abdicō (“to deny, refuse, abdicate”), from both ab- (“of, from, by”), from Latin ab (“from, away from, on, in”), from Proto-Italic *ab, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epó (“off, away”) + and from dicō (“to dedicate, devote”), possibly from *dex, from Proto-Indo-European *deyḱ-s, from *deyḱ- (“to point out”). Last part from Old Norse -ingr m, -ingi m, -ing f, from Proto-Germanic *-ingō, *-ungō.

1004994.etyen:
PIE word
 *werdʰom
Compound of j (“the letter j”) + verb (“verb”), literally “j-verb”.
The first element refers to the j (“letter j”) characteristic of the infinitive of this Nynorsk verb class. The second element, verb (“verb”), is borrowed from Latin verbum (“word; verb”), from Proto-Italic *werðom (“word”), from Proto-Indo-European *werdʰom (“word”), ultimately from *werh₁- (“to speak, say”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk j-verb (“j-verb”).
